prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be referred to as the claimant for this, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the collision happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in League City, Texas, near a shopping center entrance.
Q: What were you doing right before it happened?
A: I was driving home from the grocery store. It was a clear afternoon and traffic was light.
Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what was the other vehicle doing?
A: I was heading north. The other car was coming south and it drifted into my lane. We ended up nose to nose, but we weren't going very fast. Maybe fifteen miles an hour at most, I'd guess.
Q: Did you or the other driver brake or swerve?
A: I braked hard and turned the wheel to the right, but there wasn't enough room. The impact was more of a jolt than a crash.
Q: Were there any airbags deployed in your vehicle?
A: No, they didn't go off. My car was still drivable, so I pulled onto the shoulder.
Q: Did you feel any injuries at the scene?
A: Not right away. I felt stiff in my neck that evening, and by the next morning it was sore and I had trouble turning my head to check my blind spot.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care two days later. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral for physical therapy.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still having stiffness when I drive and when I sleep. I'm working with my doctor on it.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
